This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston. The U.S. air travel system is slowly
getting back up to speed after Friday's nationwide ground stop. NPR's Joel Rose
reports aviation regulators are laying the blame for the telecom meltdown on a federal contractor.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says the massive outage that brought the U.S.
aviation system to its knees started with a routine router upgrade by contractor L3 Harris
Technologies. This was an FAA system that didn't meet the moment. A contractor didn't meet the
moment or the equipment didn't meet the moment and caused the outages. The Federal Aviation
Administration says the work was part of the transition from older copper wire to fiber optic
cable. In a statement, L3 Harris says it is supporting the FAA's investigation into what
went wrong and that it takes the impact on airlines and travelers seriously.
Joel Rose, NPR News, Washington. Thousands of flights across the country are still delayed or
canceled following Friday's ground stop. Christopher Alum from member station KQED spoke to travelers
from San Francisco International Airport. A long line snakes around empty carousels at baggage
claim. Travelers were eager to share their frustrations. This is the United States of America.
This shouldn't not be happening to these people. We have teachers that need to get back to their
students. Everyone's bags were everywhere. No one was checking. Anyone could walk up to anyone's bag
and there were like hundreds of bags downstairs. Just exhausted, tired. Yeah, a bit frustrated,
of course, as well. But the main thing is we get home all right. That was Sylvia Garcia,
Lindsay Smith and Tim Fischl. For NPR News, I'm Christopher Alum in San Francisco. A new law
in Florida that bans cities from using taxpayer dollars to support diversity initiatives has led
to its first big cancellation, the St. Patrick's Day Parade. NPR's Marissa Lang reports the event
has been a nearly 60 year tradition. Florida's newest anti-DEI law has come for one of the most
popular events of the year in Delray Beach. Mayor Tom Carney, a Republican, said the law bans local
governments from funding any celebrations of diversity. That means next year the city will
no longer be sponsoring pride or its popular St. Patrick's Day Parade. I received so many phone
calls and texts and people telling me the social media was blowing up saying why are we getting
rid of the St. Patrick's Day Parade? In a post on X this week, Florida's Republican Governor Ron
DeSantis accused Delray Beach of weaponizing the new law to make a political point. The mayor has
rejected this characterization. He's focused instead on finding new ways to make sure the show
can go on. We should just go ahead and have it but we'll get it privately funded. Already he's
received some offers. Marissa J. Lang, NPR News. This is NPR News in Washington.
Investigators have recovered the voyage data recorder from the tanker that struck a docked
cruise ship in New Orleans Friday, injuring 32 people. The port of New Orleans is suing,
alleging at least a million dollars in damage to its terminal. The judge has authorized federal
agents to take control of the tanker. The Coast Guard says removing the capsize cruise ship could
take weeks. Holiday dinners and parties will be taking place over the next two months and that
means lots of food. According to the Environmental Protection Agency, the average American household
wastes nearly $3,000 a year on uneaten food. Scott Moscioni from member station WYPR has tips on how
to avoid waste and save money. The U.S. wastes about 30% of the food supply and half of that
comes from households, according to Johns Hopkins environmental health researcher Ronnie Neff.
But there are ways to get some of that back. Use your freezer. There's a lot of things that
can be frozen that, you know, most people don't recognize. Ness says to remember to label those
foods and consider having a day for eating leftover meals each week to ensure everything
gets gobbled up. Another way to reduce waste is using online food calculators to make portions
suitable for the number of guests at a party. For NPR News, I'm Scott Moscioni in Baltimore.
Children with autism got a chance to score touchdowns on the Philadelphia Eagles home
field on Saturday. The nonprofit Camp for Kids organized the event during a Temple University
football game at Lincoln Financial Field. The children stepped onto the field and took their
own turns reaching the end zone. Organizers say the goal was to give them a chance to be part
of the game. This is NPR. This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners
